prerequisites: Secure handling of one's own PC (requirements Intel/AMD 64, 16GB RAM, 500GB SSD, OS Linux/MacOS/Windows). Students are provided with a ready-to-use image of a virtual machine for self-study at home, which can be executed on all Intel/AMD platforms using VirtualBox or other common hypervisors. This image is also available in the PC pools of the faculty.

learning_outcomes.text: Name general terms of computer science.
Describe the historical development of programming languages in outline.
Logically grasp simple problems and independently create an algorithmic solution.
Implement predefined or self-developed algorithms in a higher imperative programming language, especially in C.
Use operating system services and a development environment.
Discuss and create solutions for programming tasks alone or together in small teams.
Understand given code parts and independently make extensions in the code.
Create more extensive C programs (between 500 - 2000 lines of code).
Operate the essential components of a development environment (Editor, Compiler, Debugger and Build-Tool).
Solve programming tasks alone or together in small teams.
Use the GIT tool for version control of source code with repositories on the PC and in the cloud.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts of computer science
Phases and tools of software development
Basic concepts and principles of imperative programming
Programming languages (general and specifically C language)
Control flow
Primitive data types in C
Separate compilation and development environment (Editor, Build-Tool, Debugger)
Enumerations and data type bool
Functions, subroutine technique, parameter passing, stack setup and teardown
Records
Arrays
Pointers
Static and dynamic memory objects, validity, visibility and lifetime
Linked lists and other memory structures
String functions of the standard library
Creation of an interactive game (Worm) with simple symbolic graphics based on the Curses-library
Working with a simple, non-integrated development environment in the console (Editor, Compiler, Debugger)
Using a Linux-Workstation for the development of C-programs
Working in a remote session via SSH
Using a simple Build-Tool (GNU make)
Using RCS GIT with repositories on your own computer and in the cloud

Programming in the C language is done based on a virtual Linux-machine, whose image is pre-installed in all computer pools of the faculty. This image can also be copied by all students and used on their own PC. Only OpenSource software is used in the virtual machine, so that the image of the virtual machine can be copied and distributed as often as desired.

assessment_methods.method: practical examination (acquisition of four attestations through programming tasks in C)

assessment_rules: Successful completion of the practical examination (2.2) is a prerequisite for participation in the written examination (2.1). In the practical training, several attestations (programming tasks in C) must be acquired. Upon successful completion of the task, an attestation is awarded by the lecturer. Solutions may and should be worked out in small groups to promote social and technical competence. A total of four tasks covering essential lecture topics must be completed. The finished solutions are to be presented individually within a fixed schedule (one attestation every 14 days), including answering questions about the solution concept and the created program. Only if all four attestations are acquired in time is the performance record considered fulfilled.
